scope: Third dance source, VLM planner v1.2 balanced candidates A/B/C, each executed with native DepthDirector Stage2 and Stage3; comparison is within these three, not a user-labelled or global optimum.
integrity: All three passed dd_feedback.collect native video hash, action frame count, Stage2 endpoint anchor, and fixed Stage3 camera checks; see v12_balanced_case15_abc_native_integrity.json.
review_method: Manual source-vs-generated image comparison at 10 evenly distributed moments per Stage3 action window, plus all-frame official DWPose observations and strict native integrity checks. The visual judgement covers the whole Stage3 window, and DWPose is only auxiliary 2D evidence; continuous human playback and user preference remain unverified.

A.vlm_plan: source highlight f101, right 30 degrees, Stage2 4 s, Stage3 25 frames/1.00 s
A.stage2: Human remains fully visible and the plain studio stays structurally intact; parallax/camera movement is hard to perceive against the nearly featureless background.
A.stage3_human_scene: Human remains recognizable throughout all sampled moments, with scene intact. Face, hands, and garment become visibly softer/blurred late in the segment.
A.stage3_action: Arms move toward/behind the head and legs progress broadly in the source sequence; pose details and the second half are imperfect, including some lower-body mismatch.
A.stage3_temporal: No sampled catastrophic disappearance or background melting; blur increases toward the end.
A.all_frame_dwpose: 25/25 source and 25/25 generated human detection, 17.0/17 mean accepted body joints in both; pelvis-relative 2D core motion-delta MAE 0.125, limb 0.113 body units. These values do not establish 3D or perceptual equivalence.
A.holistic_result: Provisional strongest of the three executed plans, with visible late blur and limited demonstrable bullet-time orbit effect. Not certified as best frame, best angle, or final-quality pass.

B.vlm_plan: source highlight f271, left 45 degrees, Stage2 6 s, Stage3 33 frames/1.32 s
B.stage2: Human remains mostly visible, but a strong dark wall/pillar appears at the right edge during the orbit, changing composition.
B.stage3_human_scene: Person remains recognizable early, becomes pale/soft or ghosted from the middle, then partly regains definition; the side wall persists.
B.stage3_action: Generated arms largely remain near/behind the head while source arms swing substantially in the latter half; pose/action timing diverges.
B.stage3_temporal: Visible person sharpness/opacity instability through the middle and end.
B.all_frame_dwpose: 33/33 source and generated human detection, but mean accepted joints decrease from 16.88 to 15.58; core motion-delta MAE 0.189, limb 0.619 body units. Cross-view 2D metric is auxiliary.
B.holistic_result: Stage3 quality failure on action fidelity and temporal appearance stability.

C.vlm_plan: source highlight f577, right 20 degrees, Stage2 2.5 s, Stage3 17 frames/0.68 s
C.stage2: Human and plain studio remain framed; orbit cue is weak against blank background.
C.stage3_human_scene: Person progressively fades into the pale background, becoming a low-contrast ghost by the end, despite stable scene geometry.
C.stage3_action: The source hand/arm swings across the body; generated arm and body are almost static after the first frames.
C.stage3_temporal: Continuous loss of contrast and detail over the 17-frame window.
C.all_frame_dwpose: 17/17 source and generated human detection, but mean accepted joints decrease from 16.88 to 15.24; core motion-delta MAE 0.088, limb 0.483 body units. The relatively small core error misses the obvious visual fading and arm-action failure.
C.holistic_result: Clear Stage3 quality failure despite short duration and high valid-mesh coverage.

relative_judgement: A is visually stronger than B and C among these executed plans, but the comparison confounds selected time, angle, orbit duration, and action length. There is no user-labelled best frame and no evidence of global optimality. Final angle should be decided by VLM with real output feedback, subject to accurate visual reasoning and human review.
planner_reason_correction: The VLM description of A f101 as both feet airborne with arms up is false: the source image shows one foot grounded, one knee lifted, and arms below an overhead position. This invalidates that stated reason, not necessarily candidate A itself.

vlm_native_feedback.agreement: Relative preference A agrees with manual dense-sample review.
vlm_native_feedback.disagreement: Feedback awards A 5/5 on every dimension and says all Stage3 frames match source precisely, although it inspected only selected frames and late face/hand blur plus pose differences are visible. Its B/C quality failures are directionally consistent, but precise claims of melting or anatomy should be checked against images.
vlm_native_feedback.status: Auxiliary model judgement, not human ground truth or final-quality certification.

vlm_dense_feedback.invalid_evidence: Candidate C has only 17 Stage3 frames (f0..f16), yet feedback references frame 24. It also gives A 5/5 for every dimension and denies visible late blur.
vlm_dense_feedback.conclusion: More sampled frames did not make this VLM feedback reliable enough for final quality acceptance or angle optimality.
